# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 65/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. High = (16.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 65.

This is an Astro site with three pages (`/`, `/moorings`, `/contact`), and I read all of them. The basics are in place: the pages are static HTML, titles, descriptions and `lang` are set, and the sitemap is linked from robots.txt. The score is held back by two AI search crawlers blocked in robots.txt, two broken JSON-LD blocks, a canonical tag that points every page at the home page, and a snippet restriction set by default.

Nothing is left unknown, because everything is decided in the repository. This was read from code and not checked on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in, or confirm that blocking them is intended (GEO-009)
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are barred from the whole site, so those tools can't read any of your pages.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77/100. I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json`. If blocking them is deliberate, tell me and I'll set `policy.aiSearchCrawlers` to match. The rule then becomes Clear, and the score is the same.

### 2. Fix the two broken JSON-LD blocks (GEO-004)
- **Why it matters:** Structured data (JSON-LD) labels what a page is. Broken labels get ignored.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:**
  - `" ": {` where the FAQ answer property `acceptedAnswer` should be, so the first Question has no answer.
  - `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` has a trailing comma, which is invalid JSON.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 73/100.

### 3. Remove the default `max-snippet:0` (GEO-017)
- **Why it matters:** `max-snippet:0` tells search tools not to quote your page. That works against being found.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `<meta name="robots" content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"} />`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 71/100. The next-largest item is GEO-015 (the canonical tag), which is also worth about 1.3 points. Fixing both takes the score to 72 after item 1, or to 78 after items 1 and 2.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny file (3 of 3 routes) |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access policy says | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4-8`, blocked site-wide (0 of 3) |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/contact.astro:4` has `robots="noindex"` yet is in the sitemap and nav (2 of 3 clear) |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the right origin | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:8` hardcodes `https://harbor.example/` for every page (1 of 3 clear) |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Not run | Astro static output; `Newsletter` is server-rendered before hydration (3 of 3) |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and is complete | Problem | Not run | `src/data/faq.json:8`, `src/pages/moorings.astro:9` (0 of 2 routes with JSON-LD) |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap valid and discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, `public/robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:4-7`; each page passes its own values (3 of 3) |
| GEO-016 | Routes reachable via plain links | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:12`, plain `<a href>` (3 of 3) |
| GEO-017 | No snippet block conflicting with AI search | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`, default applies to `/` and `/moorings` (1 of 3 clear) |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read `Base.astro` and `Newsletter.jsx`; input is labelled, button has text, no images |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only, unscored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found; optional |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info only, unscored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app |

Two more details on the Problems:
- **GEO-014:** Either make `/contact` indexable, or take it out of the sitemap and nav.
- **GEO-015:** Because `/contact` is noindex, its canonical pointing at `/` is harmless, but `/moorings` pointing at `/` tells search engines it's a duplicate of the home page.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which compares real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** whether pages really answer 200, and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is added by your host, can only be confirmed with a live scan.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. This drives GEO-009 and GEO-017.
- Because that policy is assumed and not declared, I did not apply the 40-point cap for a site-wide crawler block. If you confirm you want those crawlers allowed, the cap would apply and the score would be 40 until item 1 is fixed.
- The origin is `https://harbor.example`, taken from the sitemap and robots.txt.
- Separately, blocking training crawlers such as `GPTBot` is a different choice. Nothing here blocks them, and I did not count that.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
